answers.note: Игуасу в Аргентине вместе с соседним бразильским парком сохраняет значительный остаток Атлантического леса.

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: APN L46-L48 names Garganta del Diablo as principal Iguazu fall; L94 and park sidebar L115-L129 explicitly locate the activities within Parque Nacional Iguazu. UNESCO303 L43/L63 establishes Argentine park/protection context. Prompt asks the Argentine park, so unqualified Iguasu resolves to it; explicit Brazil alternative is a distinct sister park, while Plitvice is Croatia and Vatnajokull Iceland. The prompt never supplies the Iguazu name, so this is not simply matching an already-given name/country.

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.literal: Это Игуасу. Река образует сотни отдельных каскадов среди субтропического леса.
sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: The first sentence names Iguasu; UNESCO303 L43-L55 describes the river’s cataracts amid subtropical forest. The official municipal attraction L269-L270 gives more than275 falls and forest, supporting the retained broad hundreds of cascades without treating a precise variable count as constant. Both sentences describe the same transboundary waterfall system, not an exclusive bank division.

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: UNESCO303 L46/L48 explicitly says Argentine Iguazu with neighboring Brazilian property preserves a significant Atlantic Forest remnant. UNESCO355 L51/L58 corroborates the contiguous major Interior Atlantic Forest remnants. This is new conservation/ecosystem knowledge about the chosen park beyond its protecting Devil’s Throat.

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.literal: Бразильский национальный парк Игуасу находится в штате Парана и граничит с аргентинским парком.
sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: UNESCO355 L51 explicitly states Iguaçu in Paraná, southern Brazil, adjacent to Argentina’s Iguazu. The note exactly describes that named Brazilian option, without pretending Devil’s Throat belongs only to Brazil or asserting an unsupported east-bank simplification.

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.literal: Плитвицкие озёра — хорватский парк с каскадом озёр, разделённых природными травертиновыми плотинами.
sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: UNESCO98 L50 identifies Croatia and interconnected lake/waterfall system; L5/L51-L61 explains naturally deposited travertine/tufa barriers forming dams. The note accurately gives its own park/geological fact, not the queried Argentine waterfall relation.

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.literal: Ватнайёкюдль — исландский парк вокруг одноимённого ледника и действующих вулканов подо льдом.
sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: UNESCO1604 L4/L38 places the park and its namesake ice cap in Iceland, L39-L40 describes subglacial volcanoes including active ones. The note retains those facts and makes no unestablished largest-country-glacier ranking.

absoluteLevel.ground: Editorial absolute calibration under the allowed large-cultural-demographic criterion: Iguazu/Garganta del Diablo is a major iconic natural landmark in Argentina and Brazil, plausibly common cultural adult knowledge there, not merely a specialist protected-area fortress/date detail. This is an editorial inference about that broad audience, not a survey claim that most Russian adults or every adult knows it. The prompt does not give Iguazu’s name; recognizing the named main fall/Argentine park supplies the fact. Brazil is a credible sister-park confusion; Plitvice and Vatnajokull are real protected water landscapes and can be narrowed by geographic familiarity.
